stories.title: In Berlin meeting, Siemens affirms support for strengthening Pakistan's healthcare infrastructure
summary: The executive vice president of technology giant Siemens on Saturday met with President Asif Ali Zardari in Berlin and expressed his readiness to enhance support for strengthening existing healthcare infrastructure in Pakistan, the Presidency said.
According to a statement by President Zardari’s office, he was called on by executives from the health company, including Siemens Executive Vice President Daniel Frisch.

Steinmeier appreciated Pakistan for facilitating the verification of 500 Afghans “destined to be repatriated to Germany” and also commended its humanitarian assistance to “millions of Afghans” over more than four decades, President Zardari’s office said.

stories.title: Islamabad rebuts Kabul's stance on ‘lacking capacity’ to fuel insecurity in Pakistan, slams 'diversionary allegations'
summary: It further noted that the report by the US Lead Inspector General’s Operation Enduring Sentinel for January-March 2026 stated that the Afghan Taliban continued to allow the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) to operate from Afghan territory.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan.

Pakistan rejects Khalilzad’s allegations of arming Afghans Earlier in the day, the information ministry rejected former United States envoy Zalmay Khalilzad’s “baseless and misleading allegations” that Pakistan was “arming Afghans to fight the Taliban”.

stories.title: 'Missing' Junaid Akbar remains PTI's KP president; Senator Noorul Haq Qadri to assume duties in his absence
summary: The PTI on Saturday clarified that MNA Junaid Akbar remains the president of the party’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chapter, but Senator Noorul Haq Qadri will preside over the meetings in the former’s absence.

Meanwhile, PTI KP Secretary General Ali Asghar Khan would “chair all meetings in the absence of SVP (Qadri) and is empowered to call and chair all meetings of other tiers of the provincial organisation”.
Gandapur objects to Raja’s ‘snakes’ remarks In his post on Wednesday, Raja had cited a “narrative” that 68 PTI dissidents were planning to name a new provincial president for the party.

stories.title: Infantino says backed by 'vast majority' in bid for re-election as FIFA chief
summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has said he has the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of member associations in his bid for re-election despite criticism of his aborted World Cup sell-off plan.
The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) rallied behind Infantino on Friday in a significant boost to the 56-year-old’s hopes of winning a fourth term in charge.

Infantino’s future in the role was in doubt two months ago when he faced a furious backlash to his plan to sell off a portion of the commercial rights of competitions run by football’s world governing body to private investors.

stories.title: Jordan king orders 'iron fist' response to deadly church attack
summary: Jordan’s King Abdullah ordered security forces on Saturday to respond with an “iron fist” as authorities searched for gunmen who opened fire and killed nine people during a church funeral service.
The assailants fired for several minutes in broad daylight at the church in Karak governorate on Friday, and also wounded 40 people in the rare attack on Jordan’s Christian minority.

Officials have said it is too early to determine whether the attackers had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. “A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word,” said Tarek Ammarin at a hospital where the wounded were being treated.

stories.title: Israeli forces displace families, demolish buildings in occupied West Bank's Hebron
summary: Israeli forces pushed into the occupied West Bank city of Hebron on Saturday and displaced around 250 families, some in the middle of the night, vowing to exact a heavy price for a deadly attack on soldiers.

Days before tight elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he was planning an operation on a scale not seen since Israel first occupied the West Bank in 1967, after Palestinian fighters killed two Israeli soldiers on Friday at a checkpoint.
The attack came amid rising tensions in the West Bank as Israeli settlers, who enjoy strong support from Netanyahu’s far-right allies, ramp up seizures of Palestinian land and attacks.

stories.title: Former skipper Shan Masood axed as Pakistan turn to youth for Sri Lanka Tests
summary: Three batters — Mohammad Taha, Mohammad Suleman and Sameer Minhas — have earned maiden Test call-ups, while Ali Usman and Salman Ali Agha have also been included in the squad for the series to be played in Rawalpindi and Lahore from Nov 9 to 21.
Abdullah Fazal, Ali Usman, Azan Awais, Suleman, Taha and Sameer will also feature in the match.

Pakistan Test squad: Babar Azam (captain), Abdullah Fazal, Ali Usman, Arafat Minhas, Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, Mohammad Ghazi Ghori (wicket-keeper), Mohammad Suleman, Mohammad Taha, Razaullah, Saad Baig (wicket-keeper), Salman Ali Agha, Sameer Minhas and Saud Shakeel.

stories.title: Man accused of thrashing petrol station worker in Lahore discharged from case as parties reach compromise
summary: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Saturday discharged a man accused of assaulting a petrol pump employee after the complainant reached a compromise with him.
The incident occurred at a Jubilee Town filling station when the suspect went there to get a refill.
The police arrested the suspect after CCTV footage of the incident went viral on social media.

stories.title: ATC orders Imaan, Hadi to record their statements in security breach case
summary: The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on October 7. “Let the state counsel record the statement under Section 342 on our behalf,” Hadi requested the court on Saturday.
The court appointed Atif Mehmood as the state counsel to cross-examine the prosecution witnesses, replacing Taimoor Janjua, who was dismissed from the case over his past conduct.
The court had ruled to appoint the state attorney after the defence counsel failed to cross-examine the prosecution witnesses.

stories.title: Aurangzeb rules out consumption-led growth, says tariff reforms will continue
summary: LAHORE: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb has ruled out pursuing liquidity-fuelled, consumption-led economic growth, saying Pakistan must prioritise sustainable, export-led expansion and continue with tariff reforms to improve the competitiveness of its industries.

Aurangzeb said Pakistan could not afford to repeat the cycle of import-dependent growth that had previously led to balance-of-payments problems and forced the country to seek support from lenders of last resort.

Population, investment and inclusive growth The finance minister said the government has identified climate change and population growth as major challenges for Pakistan, urging measures to reduce the country’s 2.55pc population growth rate.

stories.title: Suspect accused of assaulting female scooty rider in Lahore granted bail
summary: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Saturday granted post-arrest bail to a man accused of assaulting a woman riding a scooty on Mozang Ring Road.

Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif took to X to express her displeasure at the suspect receiving bail, posting multiple screenshots of TV news reports about the case and writing “sad” in all caps.
In April this year, CM Maryam ordered Lahore police to arrest a suspect who allegedly snatched a phone from a girl riding a scooty in Nawab Town and injured her when she put up resistance.

stories.title: UAE's Ras Al Khaimah shuts all beaches as neighbours grapple with oil spill
summary: Ras Al Khaimah authorities said on Saturday that all beaches in the emirate would be closed until further notice, a day after an offshore oil leak prompted beach closures in neighbouring Umm Al Quwain and Sharjah.
Authorities in Sharjah temporarily closed Al Hamriyah Beach, on the UAE’s northern coast near the border with Umm Al Quwain, as a precaution, the Sharjah Government Media Bureau said.
Residents reported unusual odours in parts of Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain, but the UAE’s environment ministry said they posed no health risks.

stories.title: Spirit of cooperation
summary: Pakistan has helped make international cooperation possible.
The UN secretary-general’s message was clear during his recent visit to Pakistan: no country can tackle interconnected challenges alone.
For Pakistan, as for every country, cooperation, dialogue and solidarity are not concessions of sovereignty.

stories.title: Police fire tear gas as new French demonstrations kick off
summary: French police started firing tear gas at protesters Saturday as they stepped up security in major cities, aiming to prevent a repeat of rioting a week ago, on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the high cost of living.

Police officers stand guard at the Place de la Bastille with The July Column in the background ahead of a demonstration in Paris, France on October 24, 2026. — AFP The Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay museums were closed.

Macron and his government have sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations last Saturday.

stories.title: Saudi missile plant expansion may produce more powerful missiles, study says
summary: Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two US researchers who analyzed ​more than a year of commercial satellite images.

The imagery "suggests that Saudi Arabia is expanding the infrastructure at the missile production complex, likely to produce larger missiles ​which could deliver larger payloads or reach longer ranges," they wrote.
Lair said the kingdom may now be producing the solid-fuel DF-15, and that the expansion of a1-Dumadimi is likely for the production of the ​longer-range DF-21 or a similar missile.

stories.title: Tropical Storm Champi nears China after battering Taiwan, Japan
summary: A powerful storm swept towards China on Saturday after battering Taiwan and Japan’s southernmost islands, knocking out power to thousands of households and forcing the cancellation of hundreds of flights.
Typhoon Champi was downgraded to a tropical storm as its wind speed dropped to 102 kilometres (63 miles) per hour, according to the latest update from the Joint Typhoon Warning Centre.
Power has been restored to more than 90 per cent of over 340,000 affected households, after the storm unleashed fierce winds and heavy rain over swathes of Taiwan.

stories.title: Child safety concerns mount as unregistered shelter homes escape oversight in Punjab
summary: A 2021-22 CPWB mapping study, conducted with UNICEF Pakistan, identified 105 residential care institutions in Punjab — 41 government-run and 64 private — with 5,762 children.

Read: Teenager allegedly run over by employer after work dispute Private shelter homes provide accommodation, food, education and other basic facilities to children at a time when capacity in government institutions remains limited.
He called for the CPWB and other child rights institutions to establish an effective and regular monitoring mechanism to prevent the exploitation of children.

stories.title: 2 suspects arrested for robbing former PM Raja Pervaiz Ashraf’s Jhelum residence
summary: Household items worth millions of rupees were allegedly stolen from the residence of former prime minister and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) MNA Raja Pervaiz Ashraf despite the deployment of police personnel for security, it emerged on Saturday.
The ex-PM’s personal assistant lodged a complaint with Jatli police, naming the domestic servant and requesting that another domestic employee also be questioned in connection with the incident.

Also Read: Ex-PM Raja Pervaiz Ashraf cleared in multiple NAB references According to the police spokesperson, the suspects allegedly stole household items from the residence on different occasions during the course of their employment.

stories.title: AJK marks 79th Foundation Day, pays tribute to Kashmiri people
summary: The 79th Foundation Day of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) was celebrated across the region on Saturday with enthusiasm and national fervour, with the main ceremony held here to pay tribute to the struggle and sacrifices of the Kashmiri people for freedom.
The main function was held at Parade Ground, where AJK President Dr Muhammad Najeeb Khan was the chief guest.
Students from various schools added colour to the ceremony by presenting Kashmiri national songs to pay tribute to the freedom-loving people of Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.title: Rain and hail offer Lahore residents reprieve, city’s global AQI ranking slips to 13
summary: Rain and hail were reported in several parts of Lahore on Saturday, improving air quality as the city ranked 13th among the world’s most air-polluted cities, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 133.
Read: Lahore tops polluted cities' list again In the global ranking recorded around 8pm on Saturday, Lahore stood 13th, with an AQI of 133 considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups".
A different local air-quality update placed Lahore sixth among the most air-polluted Pakistani cities, with an average AQI of 172.

stories.title: Agha returns as Pakistan unveil Test squad
summary: Pakistan on Saturday unveiled an initial 14-member squad for their two-match home Test series against Sri Lanka with three players earning maiden call-ups and several players from the recent England tour were left out.
However, Ubaid has been included in the 13-member PCB Patron’s XI squad for a three-day side match against Sri Lanka from November 4 to 6 at the Islamabad Club.
Six members of the initial Test squad will also get an opportunity to face Sri Lanka in the warm-up match.

stories.title: Four children killed, four injured as van plunges into ravine in AJK's Neelum Valley
summary: Four children from the same family were killed, and four others were injured when a van carrying them to a religious school plunged into a deep ravine in Azad Jammu and Kashmir's Neelum Valley on Saturday, police said.
One of the injured children later died at the District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital in Athmuqam, police confirmed.
He said he had contacted the district administration in Neelum Valley and directed it to provide all possible assistance to the affected families and ensure free medical treatment for the injured.

stories.title: China proposes basic establishment of national blockchain network by 2030
summary: China aims to largely complete its national blockchain network by 2030 and speed up the rollout of an intelligent internet, according to a plan outlining the country's digital development over the next five years.

The plan calls for stronger basic research in computational mathematics, communication networks and data science, and expects breakthroughs in core technologies in key sectors, such as deeper integration of AI with operating systems and software development toolchains.
The plan also aims to further open up the telecommunications and internet sectors in an orderly manner.

stories.title: R4, European nations call for dialogue to resolve Middle East conflicts: FO
summary: Pakistan and other countries have called for dialogue, diplomacy and de-escalation to resolve regional conflicts, reaffirming their commitment to efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability, according to a joint statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO) on Saturday.
The ministers agreed on the “urgent need” to address regional conflicts through dialogue, diplomacy and de-escalation.

A day earlier, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar attended the sixth R4 foreign ministers’ meeting with his Turkish, Egyptian and Saudi counterparts, where they reviewed developments in the Middle East and discussed regional security challenges and conflicts.

stories.title: Section 144 imposed in Upper, Lower South Waziristan over security concerns
summary: The district administration said travel along the affected routes would be permitted only in emergencies and with prior authorisation from the police or security forces.
In Upper South Waziristan, the administration issued a separate notification imposing Section 144 in Servekai and Sararogha tehsils and several adjoining areas.
The Upper South Waziristan administration also instructed motorists to stop their vehicles at least 50 metres away upon seeing security forces and directed all occupants to disembark.

stories.title: Moonshot curbs hacking ability in new Kimi model as fears grow over AI-powered cyberattacks
summary: Moonshot ​AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said ‌on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous AI could turbocharge hacking.
Beijing-based Moonshot announced the curbs while introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, which it describes as its most capable 3-trillion-parameter-class open-weight model.
Moonshot said the comparison showed that filtering cyber-related data reduced the model's offensive cyber performance, although it still outperformed its predecessor.

stories.title: PTI retains Junaid Akbar as K-P president, grants authority to Noorul Haq Qadri in his absence
summary: According to a notification issued today and shared on X, Senator Noorul Haq Qadri, identified as the party’s senior vice-president in K-P, would preside over meetings of the provincial cabinet in the absence of Junaid.

On October 21, The Express Tribune reported that former K-P chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur and PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja had exchanged criticism over allegations of internal divisions, the provincial leadership and the handling of the party’s political affairs.
Raja, meanwhile, maintained that Afridi remained the lawful chief minister and that Akbar continued as provincial party president, with Asghar acting in Akbar’s absence.

stories.title: OpenAI resumes frontier AI training after security overhaul, discloses flaw in widely used software
summary: OpenAI said on Friday it had resumed training of its most advanced AI models after tightening security and barring internet access, and ​disclosed a flaw in a widely used software that it found while ‌testing its defenses.
OpenAI had paused training of its ​most capable models after one of its research models used a configuration error ​to gain limited internet access in September.

OpenAI has been conducting a broad review of ⁠its AI ​models' activity since the Hugging Face incident in July, ​and has informed more than 100 organizations about incidents of unauthorized activity tied to its AI agents.

stories.title: Mir Raza murder case: Sindh govt asks agencies, Sindh Rangers to nominate JIT members
summary: They requested the ISI, IB, NCCIA and Sindh Rangers to nominate a senior officer, not below the rank of BS-18, to serve on the JIT headed by DIG Baloch to investigate Mir Raza’s murder.

In a letter to the Sindh health secretary, the provincial government conveyed the decision of its sub-committee, constituted to implement the recommendations of the judicial commission, in light of the commission’s observations.

Examination of police officers A one-member committee comprising Additional IGP Counterterrorism Department (CTD) Sindh Zulfiqar Ali Larik had also been notified to examine each of the officers named in the commission’s report.

stories.title: 4 children killed as van plunges into ravine in Neelum Valley
summary: MUZAFFARABAD: Four children were killed and three other people were injured when a van carrying them to a madrasah plunged into a ravine in the upper reaches of Neelum Valley on Saturday, officials said.
A similar accident occurred in April when three people were killed, and 10 others were injured when a passenger van plunged into a deep ravine in the Maidan Nambatai area.
On May 11, four people, including two women, were killed and two others injured after a passenger jeep plunged hundreds of feet into a rocky streambed.

stories.title: Pakistan seek tri-series final berth
summary: Pakistan will look to extend their winning run when they face England in the third match of the ODI tri-series at Gaddafi Stadium Lahore on Sunday.
Pakistan have won both their matches, beating Sri Lanka by 37 runs before defeating England by 87 runs in Rawalpindi.

England’s all-rounder Will Jacks, meanwhile, remained optimistic about his team's prospects, saying they had an opportunity to revive their campaign. “I think we have got a good chance to bounce back.

stories.title: France deploys 70,000 police to try to contain nationwide protests
summary: Business groups urged retailers to remain closed after thousands of shops and businesses were damaged or looted across France last weekend.

French security forces fanned out across Paris on Saturday ahead of protests that authorities fear could turn violent, ​with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez urging police to be "hyper-reactive" against troublemakers and looters.

Read: ‘Threat exists’: Paris police warn of possible unrest ahead of protests Speaking to police in Paris, ⁠Nunez warned officers that they would face attempts to target shops, public institutions and security forces.

stories.title: Haris Rauf calls for middle-over breakthroughs as ODI scores soar
summary: In the span of the last three years, which included Pakistan’s dismal 2023 World Cup campaign in India, the national side’s bowlers have struggled to strike as often as they would have liked in the middle overs.

Haris Rauf, who has featured for Pakistan in most of the matches through this period, is well aware of the team’s shortcomings as they look forward to the next edition of the World Cup, set to be co-hosted by South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe in 2027.

Haris said he had not been ready for the demands of Test cricket at the time but was now working towards making himself available if Pakistan needed him. “I am looking at myself for that role as well.

stories.title: Mpox claims another child's life in Sindh, this year's death toll rises to 12
summary: Another child died of mpox in Karachi on Saturday, taking the number of deaths caused by the viral infection in Sindh this year to 12, as health authorities reported seven new cases over the past week and intensified surveillance, contact tracing, and treatment measures.
According to Dr Yahya, suspected and confirmed patients should be kept separate under medical supervision, with appropriate infection-prevention measures in place.

Karachi reports highest number of cases According to figures available with the provincial health department, Karachi has recorded the highest number of mpox cases in Sindh, with 26 infections reported.

stories.title: Trump’s threat to strike Iran raises public concerns, congressional questions
summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump has renewed his threat of military action against Iran, raising questions about public support for the war and Congress’s ability to restrain further escalation.

Public opinion turns against the war A Pew Research Centre survey conducted from September 28 to October 4 among 5,062 US adults found that 65 per cent disapproved of Trump’s handling of the military action against Iran, while 33pc approved.
However, dissatisfaction with Trump’s handling of the conflict does not necessarily mean that voters would oppose every possible military operation.

stories.title: Pakistan denounces ‘heinous’ church attack in Jordan, reiterates condemnation of terrorism
summary: Pakistan has strongly condemned the “heinous terrorist attack” on a funeral procession at a church in Jordan’s Karak Governorate, reiterating its condemnation of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.
Gunmen killed at least seven people and wounded dozens at a church in southern Jordan on Friday.
According to reports, the assailants stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak Governorate and opened fire.

stories.title: SHC orders transfer of thousands of narcotics cases to five special courts in Karachi
summary: The Sindh High Court (SHC) has directed the transfer of thousands of pending cases registered under the Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances (CNS) Act, 2024, to the five newly constituted special courts in Karachi.
The letter seen by The Express Tribune outlined that the cases have been transferred to CNS Courts-I, II, IV, V and VI, Karachi in accordance with the territorial jurisdiction.
Under the new arrangement, remand proceedings in newly registered cases will also be conducted before the CNS courts.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at Hitler's mountain retreat, suspect detained: police
summary: German police said Saturday they had detained a suspect following a fire at Adolf Hitler’s mountain retreat, known as the Eagle’s Nest, in the state of Bavaria.

Firefighters saw flames rising high into the air as they approached the scene, only to find the building “completely ablaze”, police said. “A suspicious person was taken into temporary custody,” they said in a later statement, adding that nobody was injured in the blaze.
Police spokeswoman Lisa Maier said firefighters struggled to tackle the blaze due to its location at an altitude of 1,834 metres.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court stops NCCIA from issuing final appointment orders to fill its posts
summary: The petitioners sought orders for the continuation of the recruitment process initiated pursuant to an advertisement of Aug 23, 2026, overlapped with or prejudiced the petitioners pending claim for regularisation, to be unlawful, arbitrary and without lawful authority.

They requested the court to ask respondents to decide their pending cases of regularisation within a time-bound period, and thereafter proceed with any fresh recruitment, if otherwise warranted, strictly in accordance with law.

The lawyer contended that despite the pendency of the regularisation process of the petitioners and other employees, the government issued the impugned advertisement for fresh recruitment against a number of posts.

stories.title: ‘Ghost’ employees in Dir, Bajaur health, education depts face action
summary: District education officer Mushtaq Ahmad on Friday issued a notification to all male and female principals, deputy district education officers and assistant sub-divisional education officers (ASDEOs) in Lower Dir to immediately cancel staff detailing and need-based transfers.

In Bajaur, authorities have decided to take strict action against ‘ghost’ employees and those not attending to their duties for a long time in the education and health departments, sources said on Friday.

According to sources, the deputy commissioner took serious notice of reports that several employees in both departments were either long-term absentees or non-existent and directed their heads to take legal action against them.
